display.purpose: The "19-0" hero wordmark only. Gradient-filled via background-clip: text — a grandfathered exception, not a reusable pattern.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked eyebrows for table headers and stat captions only.

motion.name: ease-out-strong
motion.purpose: Default entrance/reveal easing across the season review and home screen.

motion.name: ease-pop
motion.purpose: Springy pop-in for rare celebratory moments (MVP card, hero icon, verdict word).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action (Start New Run, Play Again). Gold-to-orange gradient, ink-black text, scale-down press feedback.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #f9c846, #f97316); color: #0f0f13; border: none; padding: 16px 52px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 800; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.88; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f9c846; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Mode Chip
components.description: Home-screen mode selector (T20 Blast / Test Cricket / World Cup). Active chip gets an indigo border and dark gradient fill.
components.css: .ds-chip-mode { flex: 1; padding: 14px 10px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #252535; background: #111118; color: #9090a8; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.5px; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; } .ds-chip-mode--active { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1a1a3a, #0f0f1f); border-color: #4040a0; color: #fff; } .ds-chip-icon { font-size: 22px; display: block; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-chip-label { display: block; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Stat Card
components.description: Most Runs / Most Wickets style tournament stat callout.
components.css: .ds-card-stat { background: #13131f; border: 1px solid #252535; border-radius: 12px; padding: 11px 13px; } .ds-card-stat-label { font-size: 9px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 1.6px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #5858a8; margin-bottom: 5px; } .ds-card-stat-name { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 800; color: #fff; line-height: 1.1; } .ds-card-stat-val { font-size: 26px; font-weight: 900; color: #f9c846; line-height: 1; margin-top: 3px; } .ds-card-stat-sub { font-size: 10px; color: #5858a8; margin-top: 3px; }

components.name: MVP Card
components.description: The system's showcase component: gold-bordered card with a shimmer sweep and glisten glow, used once per season review to spotlight the tournament MVP.
components.html:
⭐ MVP
Mitchell Marsh
22 runs · 11 wkts
Tournament
components.css: .ds-card-mvp { position: relative; overflow: hidden; border-color: #b8922a; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #171410, #1e1a0c); border-radius: 12px; padding: 11px 13px; animation: ds-chip-glisten 2.2s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-card-mvp::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; left: -60%; width: 40%; height: 100%; background: linear-gradient(115deg, transparent 0%, rgba(255,224,140,.5) 45%, transparent 90%); transform: skewX(-20deg); animation: ds-mvp-sweep 2.8s ease-in-out infinite; animation-delay: 1s; } .ds-card-mvp .ds-card-stat-label { color: #f9c846; } .ds-card-mvp-val { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; color: #e0c060; margin-top: 4px; line-height: 1.5; } @keyframes ds-chip-glisten { 0%, 100% { box-shadow: none; filter: brightness(1); } 50% { box-shadow: 0 0 10px currentColor; filter: brightness(1.3); } } @keyframes ds-mvp-sweep { 0% { left: -60%; } 45%, 100% { left: 140%; } }

narrative.overview: 19-0 looks like a live cricket broadcast graphics package running at night — a near-black studio backdrop lit only by scoreboard gold and orange, the way a stadium floodlight cuts through darkness onto the one thing that matters: the number on the board. Every screen borrows this logic. Panels sit on ink-black surfaces with barely-there borders; nothing competes for attention until a rating, a result, or a call-to-action needs to glow. This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS/dashboard look — no cream or beige neutrals, no identical flat card grids, no tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows scaffolding every section, no gradient-text headings used as a decorative crutch (the one exception, the "19-0" hero wordmark, is a grandfathered brand asset, not a pattern to repeat elsewhere). It also rejects the stiff, overly official tone of a real governing body's site — this is a scrappy fan broadcast, not a corporate one.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black studio backdrop; light comes from content, not chrome
Gold-to-orange gradient reserved for the primary action and the brand wordmark only
Flat, borderless-feeling panels distinguished by faint 1px borders, not shadows
Color carries meaning first (green=win, red=loss, amber=draw, gold=rating) and decoration second

rules.name: The Floodlight Rule
rules.body: Gold/orange never covers more than the CTA, the wordmark, or a single highlighted stat at a time. If more than one element on screen is glowing gold, the hierarchy has broken down.

rules.name: The Broadcast Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase, tracked, dim labels are for metadata only (table headers, stat captions). The moment a label needs to carry real information, it drops to sentence case at full body weight.

rules.name: The Flat-Studio Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow for structural depth, ever. If a component needs to feel "lifted," lighten its background one tonal step and/or brighten its border — don't reach for a shadow.

dos: Do reserve Scoreboard Gold (#f9c846) for the single most important element on any given screen — a CTA, a rating, an MVP badge.
Do build depth with tonal steps (Ink Black → Card Navy → Surface Navy → Panel Black) and 1px borders, never with box-shadow.
Do use the semantic result colors consistently: green = win/positive, red = loss/negative, amber = draw/neutral, exactly as already used across match summaries and season reviews.
Do keep every core interaction (draft, pick XI, sim, result) usable one-handed on mobile, per PRODUCT.md's "One thumb, no friction" principle.
Do gate all animation behind prefers-reduced-motion, matching the pattern already built into the season-review and home-screen entrance sequences.
donts: Don't introduce cream, beige, or any warm-neutral background — this is a near-black system, full stop.
Don't add new gradient-text treatments beyond the existing "19-0" wordmark; it's a grandfathered exception, not a precedent.
Don't add tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above every new section "because landing pages do this" — reserve that treatment for table headers and stat labels only.
Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe on cards or list rows.
Don't reach for identical repeating card grids; vary layout by content type as the existing screens already do.
Don't add box-shadow-based elevation; tonal layering and borders are the only depth language this system uses.
